### Hidden Greed
Author: Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living
URL: https://insight.org/churchleaderarticle/hidden-greed
Passage: 2 Kings 5:20-27
Points:
- Hidden greed is a subtle peril tempting God's servants to seek personal gain, applause, and reward.
- Elisha refused compensation so that Naaman would recognize God's grace as entirely free.
- Gehazi second-guessed his master's spiritual wisdom and rationalized pursuing material profit.
- Deceit quickly compounded Gehazi's covetousness as he lied both to Naaman and to Elisha.
- The severe consequence of leprosy demonstrates that God demands uncompromised integrity and accountability from His servants.

### Bible Pathways 05/02/2002
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-05-or-02-or-2002-1133406.html
Passage: 2 Kings 5:26
Points:
- Gehazi convinced himself that acquiring unearned wealth through a believable lie was a victimless sin.
- Selfish greed led to deeper dishonesty as he hid the goods and falsely denied his journey to Elisha.
- Elisha confronted him with a heart-searching question about whether this was the time to pursue personal riches.
- By succumbing to covetousness, Gehazi forfeited his prophetic calling and inherited Naaman's disease.
- Believers are challenged to examine their life's true focus and choose contentment over the destructive love of money.

### Why Did Elisha Allow Naaman to Bow to an Idol?
Author: Susan Tyner
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/elisha-naaman-bow-idol/
Passage: 2 Kings 5:18-19
Points:
- Elisha's blessing of peace shows God's gentleness toward believers who navigate difficult vocational pressures in a pagan culture.
- Gehazi's downfall serves as a warning, contrasting Naaman's genuine faith with Gehazi's secret love of money and status.
- While Gehazi outwardly served the prophet, his heart bowed down to material treasures.
- God sees past outward compliance and evaluates the true posture and devotion of our hearts.
- Christians facing real-world ethical tensions should seek God in Scripture and rely on godly counsel rather than self-serving deceit.
